summary:
I wrote $HOME/projects/llm/llamacpp/benchmarking.md (359 lines). It is the only file I created or changed. Scratch copies of the fetched sources are under $SCRATCH/bench-src/. A tool notice said the file changed on disk after my first write. My later edits went through, but I did not re-read the whole file, so the lead should open it once before indexing it.

What it covers:
- **What to measure:** prefill and decode speed at several context depths, time to first token for OpenCode-size prompts, whether the prompt cache is reused between turns, the offload trade-off, VRAM and RAM use, and GPU throttling.
- **Ground rules for every run:** GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 goes before the image name, every container gets --memory with an equal --memory-swap (heavy does not cap containers), ports are published on 127.0.0.1 only, there is no restart policy, and one model runs at a time.
- **Which image has llama-bench:** checked live. llama-bench is only in the full image, ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:full-cuda-b12407, started with --bench. The server image has only llama-server and the light image only llama-cli. The b12407 image config shows CUDA 12.8.1, about 3.62 GB compressed. full-cuda-b12418 returns 404.
- **llama-bench:** a table of its options checked at b12418, plus two pitfalls. llama-bench does not place experts automatically (fit is off), and it only reserves context for the test itself, not the server's -c. The section has a gpt-oss-20b depth example and a Llama 2 7B Q4_0 run that matches the public llama.cpp CUDA scoreboard (#15013).
- **llama-server:** the fields of the timings object, the --metrics flag and the /metrics counter names, the --cache-ram default of 8192 MiB, and a standard-library Python script that measures a fresh 8k-token turn and then a follow-up turn to check cache reuse. It flags the open cache-invalidation bug on hybrid models (#30357).
- **Expert-offload sweep (--n-cpu-moe):** one container per value, -lm none, nvidia-smi and free monitoring (I checked the nvidia-smi query fields on this machine), the cgroup memory.peak file, and a final confirmation on llama-server.
- **Tuning advice:** the reddit-18-models micro-batch advice, labeled as community advice and tied to the serial expert-copy issue (#25859). The KV cache comparison at depth refers to #27623 and its fix PR #31802 (still open), and says not to use q4 KV.
- **Quality checks:** the SQL benchmark CLI, run at least three times. Using vllm bench serve against llama-server is marked as an untested candidate.
- **Community numbers:** a labeled table with the ggml-org desktop gpt-oss-20b row (tg128 204.85), the #15013 desktop RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti rows, the TechFuelHQ llama.cpp vs Ollama rows, the Gemma 4 llama-benchy table, the recalled Qwen3.6 figure and the iBlessi Ollama rows. It explains why these are upper bounds here and gives two labeled estimates to check against.
- **Results template:** two tables, plus Sources and Maintenance sections.

The review corrections are applied: the Ollama vs llama.cpp gap for gpt-oss is put down to the model conversion, the qwen3-coder spread to load-time memory state (with 74% GPU residency measured at 8k), and the #15013 desktop RTX 5080 row is credited to @Hedede. The file has no em dashes, en dashes or emoji, and paragraph prose is one sentence per line.
unverified: The full-cuda-b12407 image was not pulled, so llama-bench inside it was not run. Its presence comes from cuda.Dockerfile and tools.sh at b12418.
Whether llama-bench -hf/-hff downloads correctly inside the full image (TLS libraries, cache path) was not tested.
The /metrics endpoint's API-key behaviour when --api-key is set was not checked.
The note that the timings object is present on non-streaming /v1/chat/completions responses comes from the b12418 README example. Whether it is in streaming final chunks was not checked.
The expected decode loss from GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 is an inference, not a measurement.
The cgroup memory.peak path (system.slice/docker-<id>.scope) comes from the host-setup research record. It was not checked against a running container.
The laptop's configured DIMM speed is unknown. Only the Intel spec (DDR5-6400 dual channel, 102.4 GB/s) was used.
The TechFuelHQ llama.cpp b10507 figure (222-238 tok/s) comes from the hf-rtx5080-throughput check record. I did not re-fetch the page.
#27623: the claim that the cliff in its title was retracted comes from the baseline. I read only part of the issue thread live, and it still shows the original title.
